evidence.C1: Design features proactive hints ('A new player who stands still for 3.5 seconds is shown the walking keys') and clear job markers ('Get into the red car ahead [F]'), but no stranger has actually played it to verify the 'without reading anything twice' claim.
evidence.C2: Distinctive mood with 'neon trim', 'Sol Wheel', and district-specific palettes ('Meridian towers are aqua, coral, cream and lilac'), recognizable from screenshots.
evidence.C3: High variety with 'Six story jobs', 'six kinds' of odd jobs, cab fares, property, and police chases, though script testing showed high failure rates on Job 5 ('Heat Wave').
evidence.C4: Gate G8 passed ('HUD boxes do not overlap'), and HUD elements are context-sensitive ('stars appear only when you are wanted'), though mobile touch controls are dense.
evidence.C5: Radical transparency: 'No one else has played any version', 'No real phone or tablet has run the game yet', and 'nobody has listened to' the radio.

fixes: Conduct real user testing with strangers to verify the 'first minute' onboarding flow and fun factor, as currently only the owner and scripts have played it.
Test on real mobile hardware to validate touch control reach, heat, and frame rate, as current testing is limited to emulation.
Rebalance Job 5 (Heat Wave) difficulty, as the script only succeeded in 2 of 12 runs due to aggressive police AI and starter car limitations.

evidence.C1: Title screen shows WASD/Mouse/F/Shift/Space/M keys; first view has 'Get into the red car ahead [F]' prompt; learner phase prevents stars until first job done; first job is short and ends at Sol Wheel landmark; job beam stands 40m ahead in car's lane
evidence.C2: Four districts with distinct looks (Meridian aqua/coral towers, Sol Beach pastel hotels, Rustport rust/ochre); 86 painted walls; day/night cycle with lit windows and neon trim; Sol Wheel, Coastliner airship, moon, drifting clouds; Pretty graphics adds glow pass and vignette
evidence.C3: Six story jobs ($250-$3,500), six odd job kinds (Rush Order, Repo Run, Block Dash, Hot Parcel, Paper Round, Shadow Run), cab fares with progression, 4 properties, 15 hidden packages, 12 stunt jumps, barrel chains, 5-star wanted system, helicopter at 4 stars, perks tying activities together
evidence.C4: G8 passed (no overlaps at 3 sizes); 'quieter screen' with cash/health only by default; stars appear only when wanted; weapon line only 5s after change; pause screen has three buttons plus settings and perks; phone controls with thumb stick and labeled buttons
evidence.C5: Own city and names (G9 passed); title screen states 'not affiliated with the publisher or the series it is often compared to'; fact sheet plainly states limits: 'How the driving feels to a person' not covered, Heat Wave 2/12 success rate disclosed, only owner has played, no real phone tested

fixes: Fix Heat Wave job balance: script only finishes 2 of 12 runs because cruisers (47 m/s) outpace the starter car (44 m/s) and the player drives at 21 m/s; one-star cruisers also ram at full speed instead of braking

Add visible feedback when the player's car is about to explode: 'a car at zero health burns for 3.6 s and then blows up with the driver; nothing on screen says so, and the game does not let the player out of a car faster than 7 m/s'

Get more human playtesting beyond the single owner: 'No one else has played any version' and the owner has not commented on 2.0+; subjective feel of driving, jobs, and balance cannot be judged from scripted runs alone

evidence.C1: First view shows 'Get into the red car ahead [F]' with 'JOB 40 m' and the car visible; title screen 'shows the keys you need first'; first job ends at the Sol Wheel pier in ~28s by script, with a learner phase so 'a first minute cannot end in a burning car' or an arrest. Only residue: walking keys appear only after standing still 3.5s.
evidence.C2: Dusk shots are distinctive: neon Ferris wheel on the pier, pink sky, 'CAFÉ'/'KITE & SURF' signs, painted walls ('86 painted walls, two designs per district'). But midday street shots still read as simple low-poly boxes with flat facades; the mood is strongest at golden hour, flatter by plain day.
evidence.C3: Six story jobs, six odd-job kinds, cab fares, property, 15 packages, ramps, barrels, nitro, perks that 'tie the side activities together', heat that closes shops and cabs. Kept from 9-10 by: 'The sums are first guesses, not tuned by play', Heat Wave finished 2 of 12 script runs, and the only human verdict was 'not fun enough' / 'not good enough'.
evidence.C4: G8 passes ('no overlaps at 3 sizes'); 'the HUD is cash and health', stars and weapon line appear only contextually, money deltas shown under cash. Phone portrait stacks five-plus text lines (radio, car, district, hint, job, perk card) over the view, which does not read at a glance.
evidence.C5: G9 'own names only'; title carries the 'not affiliated' line; 'Not covered by the tests' states limits plainly: driving feel unknown, 'nobody has listened to it', no real phone, no gamepad, 'One person has played it: the owner... not fun enough', payouts are first guesses.

fixes: Get real humans playing and tune the economy and difficulty: rewards are 'first guesses, not tuned by play' and the only playtester's feedback on 1.8/1.9 was 'not fun enough'/'not good enough' with no detail; watch where the first ten minutes drag or frustrate.

Fix the Heat Wave death spiral and the silent car burn: 'a car at zero health burns for 3.6 s and then blows up with the driver; nothing on screen says so' and exit is blocked above 7 m/s; one-star cruisers also ram at full speed (only two-star brakes) - show a burn warning, allow exit, and soften one-star pursuit.
Declutter the phone HUD: portrait stacks radio station, car name, district, hint, job distance and perk card as separate lines; consolidate or stagger them the way the desktop HUD already does.
